fact: The World Bank appraisal says many Burundian ministries and agencies run their own disparate servers, making intra-government data exchange difficult in the absence of shared solutions for data hosting and interoperability.

The World Bank's US$50 million Digital Foundations Project (PAD4690) will finance a national data exchange layer, including its connection to information systems, and technical specifications for a national data exchange solution; the document does not say any platform is yet built (date is the document's published date).

On 17 November 2026 PAFEN issued an IDA-funded request for proposals (Lot 2, 15 months) for a government interoperability platform on the X-Road model, saying institutions currently work largely in silos with limited standardised data exchange.
